gene_editing.abstract: Quantitative Biology > Genomics arXiv:2611.17705 (q-bio) [Submitted on 13 Nov 2026] Title: S1Pert: Scalable Target-Specific Gene Response Prediction with System-One Intelligence Authors: Xiaoqi Sheng , Hou wang , Yan Liang , Yutong Li , Wenhao Du , Tinghe Zhang , Jiawen Liu , Hongmin Cai View a PDF of the paper titled S1Pert: Scalable Target-Specific Gene Response Prediction with System-One Intelligence, by Xiaoqi Sheng and 7 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Predicting transcriptional responses to unseen genetic perturbations is essential for extending CRISPR screens across vast target--gene combinations. However, models can achieve strong aggregate predictive performance by reproducing historical gene-level response frequencies without adequately distinguishing the effects of different perturbations. Reliable prediction at the transcriptome scale is further challenged by uncertain response labels and redundant computation across millions of target--gene pairs. We present S1Pert, a System-One framework for target-specific gene response prediction with non-autoregressive online inference. S1Pert combines directional Welch tests and equivalence testing to distinguish statistically supported responses from inconclusive observations. A frozen System-One encoder extracts reusable semantic representations of perturbation targets, query genes, and historical evidence. Compact pair-specific interactions are then computed and cached offline. A lightweight hierarchical cross-attention decoder integrates these representations with cross-target pairwise ranking and synchronized historical-evidence dropout to reduce reliance on gene-level response frequencies. Extensive experiments demonstrate that S1Pert improves target-specific response discrimination while maintaining reliable prediction and efficient inference across diverse cellular contexts. These findings highlight the potential of System-One decision learning for scalable perturbation-response prediction beyond historical gene-level response tendencies. The source code is publicly available at this https URL . Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition arXiv:2611.22418 (cs) [Submitted on 17 Nov 2026] Title: CutAgent: Creative-Gene-Driven Planning and Experience-Guided Self-Refinement for High-CTR E-commerce Advertising Video Creation Authors: Xuyue Huang , Guanbo Huang , Jiasong Feng , Run Ling , Ao Ma , Xi Zhao , Yaoyu Li , Jie Gao , Ke Cao , Wei Feng , Zhanjie Zhang , Hao Wang , Jinghe Hu View a PDF of the paper titled CutAgent: Creative-Gene-Driven Planning and Experience-Guided Self-Refinement for High-CTR E-commerce Advertising Video Creation, by Xuyue Huang and 12 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: E-commerce advertising video creation requires both high-level creative planning and reliable multi-modal production. However, existing methods often map product attributes directly to scripts or editing decisions without explicitly modeling advertising strategies, narrative structures, and production styles. They also have limited ability to reuse past production failures. To address these limitations, we propose $\textbf{CutAgent}$, a dual-agent framework that formulates advertising video creation as a Plan--Execute--Self-Evolve process. CutAgent comprises two collaborative agents, $\textbf{GeneAgent}$ and $\textbf{VideoAgent}$, connected by a structured creative gene that bridges product understanding and video production. GeneAgent maps multi-modal product inputs---textual attributes together with product images---to creative genes that specify narrative units and production rules. To train GeneAgent, we construct $\textbf{CutAgent-70K}$ with approximately 70K samples of product attributes/images, reverse-extracted creative genes, cleaned clip pools, and real-world CTR, and apply high-CTR supervised fine-tuning followed by CTR-guided GRPO. Guided by the generated gene, VideoAgent retrieves category-then-gene failure--correction experiences from a long-term memory as constraints for shot-script planning, then coordinates material retrieval, narration, subtitles, music, and timeline rendering. Independently, a reflection loop diagnoses quality defects, revises deficient production decisions, and writes verified corrections back to memory for later retrieval. Experiments on $\textbf{CutAgent-Eval}$ show that CutAgent outperforms representative baselines in e-commerce advertising video creation, achieving the highest online CTR of $\textbf{2.21\%}$. Abstract RNA predates cells, but today it “lives” inside them. Most current RNA is short-lived, folded, and often edited from its chromosomal origins, but it governs its own phenotypes. Our guiding question for this article was: How did RNA adjust its life when the RNA world era came to an end? RNA has its practical execution side in the whole-cell systems setup, serving critical functions in metabolism, compartmentalization, and in the RNA–DNA–PROTEIN network, coupling information handling and different events of macromolecule production into a self-sustaining loop. Aligning with current views of cooperation, we find that RNA life is distributed across a population of information-bearing entities persisting by compatibility, with DNA serving as a long-term memory and proteins offering the catalytic reach. We suggest that the reproduction–survival (R/S) axis, relevant to higher organisms, is also manifested by RNA in many forms, including RNA primers, mRNAs, tRNAs, and rRNAs. Each of these has contrasting, highly adapted molecular phenotypes. Ultimately, we wish to emphasize the evolutionary narrative where “RNA did not lose” in exchange for DNA genes or otherwise. Ultimately, RNA just changed strategy, and in its various forms, it has an active and critically important presence in all cells at all times.
